Added to all these sterling performances he won the Club Championship in a new Championship time of 14.11.2 and the Inter Counties 7 miles Championship at White City on August Monday. In the veteran class Bert East appears to have been quite prominent. On 31st July, he finished third in a Veterans A.C.

Backed up by McMullen, Readman and East, we succeeded in retaining the "Berman" Trophy. Our "B" team once again finished second in the Team Handicap and Len Fletcher, proving he can still show some of them the way round, finished fourteenth and was awarded the prize for the first unplaced member.
Sawyer Memorial Cup: 1st, McMullen, 15 mins. 6.6 secs; 2nd Readman, 15.25; 3rd, East, 15.42. Discus.—Powell Trophy: 1st, Bergvalds, 123 ft. 8½ ins.; 2nd, J.

Dave McMullen was our next man showing good form early in the season, with evergreen East again among them and Pat Sapcote scoring in our first team over sevens, for the first time, thus showing he has speed as well as stamina.
Our "A" Team were second in the scratch race with Harry Churcher, Bob McMullen, Bert East and Bert Clayton scoring 31 points to Highgate Harriers' 23.
East, the veteran " junior " was well up and walking in fine style, A.

Backed up by Bert East, Bob Readman and Bert Clayton, we once again succeeded in winning the scratch team race. The race marked the return of Jack Rutland to racing after a long break, and although he was fairly well down the field, it was pleasing to see him out once again.
Team Championship.—1, Belgrave Harriers, 15 points. Churcher, McMullen, Churcher, East.

John Knifton was 24th in Section A Barnes, Belderson, Beecham and Keown, 6th 7th 30th and 32nd respectively in Section B; Eglington, Cameron, McLennan, Duncan,Wilson and Doubleday between 18 and 62 in Section C; Bushman, East and Logan 14th,15th and 34th in Section D.
Geremew Wolde was always in control, allowing Portsmouth's East to snap at his heels for the first lap before turning on the power over the last couple of miles to win convincingly.

Enter Simon Jones, fighting for a spot in the National line-up and clashing with Newham’s Michael East. Ok, East turned out to be a long way short of his best – but Simon wasn’t to know that as he showed no fear and coolly cruised past all the men ahead.
